entry: Single-celled organism without a membrane-bound nucleus or other organelles. Prokaryotes are the most abundant and diverse organisms on Earth, with an estimated 4–6 × 10³⁰ cells in total. They form two of the three domains of life, [[Bacteria]] and [[Archaea]]. All reproduce asexually, usually by [[Fission (biology)|binary fission]], although horizontal gene transfer is also common. Some, such as [[Cyanobacteria]], form colonies, and microbial communities can form mats preserved in the fossil record as stromatolites. Prokaryotes are primary producers and important biodegraders in aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, and they play a part in the carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and oxygen cycles. [[Mitochondria]], absent from prokaryotes, evolved from prokaryotic endosymbionts. The last universal common ancestor, considered "prokaryote-grade," evolved around 4.09–4.33 Ga.

Titan in Greek mythology and champion of humankind. In several versions of the myth, Prometheus molded humanity from clay and defied the Olympian gods by stealing fire for mortals. Zeus condemned him to eternal torture: he was bound to a rock while an eagle ate his liver each day, and the liver regrew overnight. According to [[Hesiod]], the hero [[Heracles]] freed him. He is regarded as the father of the human arts and sciences. In the Romantic era he came to embody the risks of overreaching, and [[Mary Shelley]] gave *The Modern Prometheus* as an alternate title for *Frankenstein* (1818).

Synthetic, radioactive chemical element with atomic number 61 (symbol Pm). All of its isotopes are radioactive. It is extremely rare in nature, with only about 500–600 grams in the Earth's crust at any given time. It is one of only two radioactive elements that are both preceded and succeeded in the [[Periodic table]] by elements with stable forms, the other being [[Technetium]]. Chemically it is a [[Lanthanide]] with only one stable oxidation state, +3. In 1914 Henry Moseley found that element 61 was missing from the series of known elements. It was first produced and characterized at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in 1945, from fission products of [[Uranium]] fuel. The discoverers named it after the Titan [[Prometheus]], to symbolize both the daring and the possible misuse of human intellect. Its only isotope with practical applications is promethium-147, used in luminous paint, atomic batteries and thickness gauges. Natural promethium arises from rare decays of [[Europium]] and spontaneous fission of uranium, so most supplies are made by bombarding uranium-235 with neutrons.

Practice of frequent sexual activity with different partners, or indiscriminate choice of partners. The term can carry a moral judgment. A common example is the one-night stand, whose frequency researchers use as a marker. What counts as promiscuous varies between cultures, and different standards are often applied to men and women. Feminists have argued that a significant double standard exists; historically, stereotypes of promiscuous women have been pejorative, while male stereotypes have been more varied. A 2005 study found that promiscuous men and women are both prone to derogatory judgment. Promiscuity is common in many animal species, and in species that form pair bonds, mating outside the pair is called extra-pair copulation. A 2006 review of 59 countries found no association between regional sexual behavior and sexual-health status, while poverty and mobility were more predictive. Some studies suggest that people with multiple casual partners are more likely to be diagnosed with [[Sexually transmitted infection|sexually transmitted infections]].

Even-toed, hoofed mammal native to interior western and central North America. Though not an [[Antelope|antelope]], it is called the American antelope because it resembles Old World antelopes through parallel evolution. It is the only surviving member of the family Antilocapridae, and its closest living relatives are the [[Giraffe]] and the [[Okapi]]. Its name comes from horn sheaths that branch and have a forward-pointing tine, unlike the horns of the [[Bovidae]]. It is the fastest land mammal in the Americas, with running speeds up to 55 mph (88.5 km/h). Males have horn sheaths averaging 9.8 in (25 cm), which are shed and regrown annually. Meriwether Lewis and William Clark first formally recorded the species during their expedition of 1804–1806. Once numbering around 35 million in the early 1800s, pronghorn populations fell because of overhunting and habitat loss, then rebounded to about 1 million by 2025. The species is rated Least Concern by the IUCN.

Word or word group used in place of a noun or noun phrase. Pronouns have traditionally been regarded as one of the parts of speech, but modern theorists doubt that they form a single class, given the variety of functions they perform across languages. Subtypes include personal, possessive, reflexive and reciprocal, demonstrative, relative, interrogative and indefinite pronouns. Many pronouns depend on an antecedent for their meaning: in *That poor man looks as if he needs a new coat*, the pronoun *he* refers back to *that poor man*. Some pronouns, such as interrogative *who*, stand for nothing at all. A treatise attributed to Dionysius Thrax, dating from the 2nd century BC, listed the pronoun as one of eight parts of speech. The English name derives, through Middle French, from [[Latin]] pronomen. Some [[Linguistics|linguists]] do not agree that pronouns substitute for [[Noun|nouns]] at all.

Mass communication aimed at persuading an audience to further an agenda. Propaganda often selectively presents facts or uses loaded language to produce an emotional rather than a rational response. Historically it was a neutral term for material promoting opinions or ideologies, but in the twentieth century it became associated with manipulation. The word derives from the [[Latin]] *propagare*, meaning to spread, and from the Congregatio de Propaganda Fide, a body of the [[Catholic Church]] created in 1622 during the [[Counter-Reformation]] to propagate the faith in non-Catholic countries. Propaganda has used paintings, posters, films, radio and television, and today bots and algorithms spread fake or biased news on [[Social media]]. [[World War I]] saw mass-media campaigns that shaped public opinion and demonized enemies. In [[Nazi Germany]] and the [[Soviet Union]], propaganda enforced conformity through censorship, repetitive messaging and personality cults.

Three-carbon [[Alkane|alkane]] with the formula C₃H₈. Propane is a gas at standard temperature and pressure, but it liquefies under compression for transport and storage. It is a by-product of [[Natural gas]] processing and [[Petroleum]] refining, and a common component of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), which fuels domestic and industrial uses and low-emissions public transportation. Discovered in 1857 by the French chemist Marcellin Berthelot, it became commercially available in the U.S. by 1911. Its low boiling point of −42 °C lets it vaporize even in cold weather, which suits barbecues, portable stoves and outdoor use. Propane has lower volumetric energy density than gasoline or coal but higher gravimetric energy density, and it burns cleaner. It is also being adopted as a replacement refrigerant (R290) for [[Heat pump|heat pumps]], offering greater efficiency than R-410A and R32, at the expense of high flammability.

Physical and chemical characteristics of pure water. Water is a polar inorganic compound, and its [[Hydrogen bond|hydrogen bonds]] underlie many unusual properties. At room temperature it is a tasteless, odorless liquid, nearly colorless with an inherent hint of blue. It is the only common substance found as a solid, liquid and gas on Earth's surface. Its specific heat capacity of 4184 J/(kg·K) at 20 °C is the second highest among heteroatomic species, after [[Ammonia]]. Water reaches its maximum density at 3.98 °C and expands on freezing, so ice floats. It is amphoteric, producing both H⁺ and OH⁻ ions, and the product of their concentrations is approximately constant. Its [[Critical point (thermodynamics)|critical point]] is at 647 K and 22.064 MPa, a supercritical state that occurs rarely in nature, such as in deep hydrothermal vents.

Body of law governing ownership and tenure in property. Property law regulates the acquisition, transfer and enforcement of proprietary rights, which usually involve relationships between private individuals. Its public-law aspects include compulsory land acquisition, environmental effects, antitrust, indigenous rights, and the human rights to property and housing. Legal systems generally distinguish real property, meaning land, from personal property, which may be tangible or intangible, such as [[Intellectual property]]. Common-law property rules originated in medieval English law, developed under separate courts of equity and common law, while [[Civil law (legal system)|civil-law]] systems trace their origins to Roman law. Roman jurists conceived ownership as dominium, a near-absolute right to use, enjoy and dispose of a thing. The most significant doctrinal influence between the two traditions is the reception of the [[Trust (law)|trust]] into civilian jurisdictions.

Ad valorem tax levied on the value of property, most often real estate. A property tax is levied by the governing authority of the jurisdiction where the property lies, which may be a national government, a state, a [[County (United States)|county]] or a municipality. Multiple jurisdictions may tax the same property. Governments typically appraise each property's value and assess tax in proportion to it. Rates are expressed as a percentage or in mills (per mille). For example, a property assessed at $50,000 in a municipality with a rate of 20 mills pays $1,000 a year. Real property is often taxed by class, such as residential, commercial, industrial or vacant, and rates differ. In [[Israel]], the rate on vacant [[Apartment|apartments]] is double the rate on occupied ones. A special assessment is a different levy, relying on a "benefit" rather than market value. Before monetary systems, taxes were often paid as a percentage of crops.

Message communicated to a person, typically a prophet, by a supernatural entity. Prophecies usually contain divine will or law, or knowledge of future events, and may be revealed in visions or direct interaction with divine beings. The English noun appeared around 1225 and derives from Old French and Greek words meaning the gift of interpreting the will of God. Much of the activity of Old Testament prophets involved conditional warnings rather than fixed futures, and the [[Torah]] already addresses false prophets. Maimonides described prophecy as an emanation from God through the Active Intellect. According to the playwright [[Aeschylus]], the Titan [[Prometheus]] gave prophecy to humankind in ancient Greek tradition. In 1863, Bahá'u'lláh, founder of the [[Baháʼí Faith]], claimed to be a Manifestation of God. Skeptics cite the Latin maxim "prophecy written after the fact."

Intravenous anesthetic used to induce and maintain general anesthesia. Propofol, first marketed as Diprivan, has largely replaced sodium thiopental for inducing anesthesia. Recovery is generally quick, with less drowsiness, nausea and vomiting than with other anesthetics. It is also used to sedate intensive care patients, where it proved superior to lorazepam in effectiveness and overall cost. First synthesized in 1973 by the British veterinary anesthesiologist John B. Glen, it was introduced in the United Kingdom and New Zealand in 1986, and the FDA approved it in October 1989. It is on the [[World Health Organization]]'s List of Essential Medicines.

Electoral principle giving groups of voters seats in proportion to their votes. Proportional representation systems ensure that the party make-up of elected representatives reflects the votes cast. They approximate proportionality far better than single-member plurality voting or block voting, although exact proportionality is never achieved except by chance. In closed-list systems, seats go to parties by vote share. In open-list and candidate-based systems such as the single transferable vote, candidates are elected on personal appeal and party label. The single transferable vote is used in Ireland, [[Malta]], the Australian Senate and the Indian Rajya Sabha. These systems are also more resistant to [[Gerrymandering]].

Meaning of a declarative sentence, and bearer of truth value. Propositions are the meanings shared by sentences such as *Snow is white* and its German equivalent, and they are the objects of beliefs. True propositions describe the world as it is, while false ones do not. Researchers distinguish affirmative and negative, universal and existential, and categorical and conditional propositions. Realists hold that propositions form part of reality, a view rejected by anti-realists. Some theories define propositions as sets of possible worlds, others as structured entities built from individuals and concepts. The study of propositions began in ancient philosophy with [[Aristotle]] and the Stoics, and later involved [[William of Ockham]], [[Gottlob Frege]] and [[Bertrand Russell]]. Logicians examine their inferential patterns, while psychologists study attitudes such as belief and desire.

Branch of classical logic dealing with propositions and their relations. Also called sentential calculus or statement logic, it studies compound propositions formed with connectives for conjunction, disjunction, implication, biconditional and negation. Propositions are represented by letters called propositional variables, and the subject deals with neither quantifiers nor non-logical objects. All of its machinery is included in [[First-order logic]] and higher-order logics, which makes it their foundation. In its classical truth-functional form, each formula has exactly one truth value, and the principle of bivalence and the law of excluded middle are upheld. Chrysippus is often credited with developing a deductive system for propositional logic in the 3rd century BC. [[Gottlob Frege]]'s predicate logic built upon it, and natural deduction was invented by Gerhard Gentzen and Stanisław Jaśkowski.

Nonselective beta blocker medication. Propranolol is used to treat high blood pressure, some irregular heart rhythms, angina, essential tremor, thyrotoxicosis and infantile hemangiomas, and to prevent migraine headaches. It works by blocking β-adrenergic receptors. Common side effects include nausea, abdominal pain and constipation, and it may worsen [[Asthma]]. Patented in 1962 and approved for medical use in 1964, it is on the [[World Health Organization]]'s List of Essential Medicines. In 2023 it was the 69th most commonly prescribed medication in the United States, with more than 9 million prescriptions.

Also called propene, the second-simplest [[Alkene|alkene]] (CH₃CH=CH₂). Propylene is a colorless gas with a faint petroleum-like odor. It was discovered in 1850 by John Williams Reynolds, a student of A. W. von Hofmann, as the only gaseous product of the thermal decomposition of amyl alcohol to react with chlorine and bromine. Global production reached about 130 million metric tons in 2024, and most of it is used to make [[Polypropylene]]. The dominant production route is steam cracking of [[Naphtha]], although [[Propane]] is a common feedstock in North America. Propylene is also made by dehydrogenation of propane. Its derivatives include propylene oxide, acrylonitrile, and cumene, which is used to make [[Phenol]] and [[Acetone]].

Ordinary form of language, following conversational speech without regular rhythm. Prose differs from poetry, which is organized by rhythmic meter, rhyme or other artistic structure. Prose can range from informal everyday speech to formal academic writing, and in writing it follows typical conventions and formatting. The word entered English in the 14th century, from Old French and the Latin *prosa oratio*, meaning straightforward speech. Latin was the dominant medium for learned prose in Europe until recent times, and works by [[Francis Bacon]] and [[Baruch Spinoza]] were first published in Latin. Dante created vernacular prose in the non-metrical parts of *Vita Nuova*, written about 1293. Academic writing, journalism and fiction are usually written in prose. The critic [[T. S. Eliot]] observed that the distinction between verse and prose is clear, but that between poetry and prose is obscure.

Literary form of poetry written in prose rather than verse. It is written as paragraphs, without line breaks, but uses poetic devices such as fragmentation, compression, repetition, rhyme, metaphor and figures of speech. Because the form has few rules, it is hard to define objectively. In 17th-century Japan, [[Matsuo Bashō]] originated haibun, a form combining [[Haiku]] with prose, best exemplified by his book *Oku no Hosomichi*. In the West, prose poetry arose in early 19th-century France and Germany as a reaction against the traditional verse line. Aloysius Bertrand's *Gaspard de la Nuit* (1842) is widely regarded as the pioneering collection, and [[Charles Baudelaire]]'s *Le Spleen de Paris* (1869) contains 50 prose poems. [[Arthur Rimbaud]] and [[Stéphane Mallarmé]] followed this example.

Study of suprasegmental features of speech, such as intonation, stress, rhythm and loudness. Prosody occurs simultaneously with individual vowels and consonants, and it reflects a speaker's emotional state, the form of an utterance (statement, question or command), irony, sarcasm, and emphasis or contrast. Auditory measures of prosody include pitch, length, loudness and timbre. Acoustically these correspond to fundamental frequency, duration, intensity and spectral characteristics. English intonation is often analyzed in three aspects: the division of speech into units, the highlighting of particular words and syllables, and the choice of pitch movement, such as a fall or a rise. Prosody displays elements of language that are not encoded by [[Grammar]], punctuation or vocabulary, and prosodic features are found in all languages.

Malignancy of the [[Prostate]] gland, the most common cancer in men excluding skin cancer. Cancer arises in gland cells, most often as adenocarcinoma. Screening uses blood tests for prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and digital rectal examination. Diagnosis requires a [[Biopsy]], and the pathologist assigns a Gleason score, with higher scores indicating more dangerous tumors. Imaging assigns a stage from 1 to 4. Many tumors remain small and are managed with active surveillance, while more dangerous ones are treated with [[Radiation therapy]] or radical prostatectomy. Cancer that spreads beyond the gland is treated with hormone therapy, and castration-resistant cancer with the [[Chemotherapy]] drug docetaxel. Tumors that metastasize, most often to bones and lymph nodes, have five-year survival rates of 30–40%, while about 99% of men with low-risk tumors survive more than 10 years. The average age at diagnosis is 67.

Gland of the male reproductive system, below the bladder. The prostate is an accessory gland and a muscle-driven switch between urination and ejaculation, and it is found in all male mammals. It surrounds the [[Urethra]], and it produces a slightly alkaline, milky fluid that forms part of [[Semen]]. Its alkalinity helps neutralize vaginal acidity and prolongs the life of [[Sperm]]. The gland is about the size of a walnut and weighs about 11 grams on average. Disorders include enlargement, inflammation, infection and [[Cancer]]. The word derives from [[Ancient Greek]] *prostátēs*, meaning "one who stands before."

Artificial device used in place of a missing body part. Prostheses may restore the function of a missing body part or serve a cosmetic purpose. Body parts may be lost through trauma or disease, or be absent from birth. A person who has had an [[Amputation|amputation]] is called an amputee, and rehabilitation is coordinated by a physiatrist within a team that includes prosthetists, nurses and therapists. Prostheses can be made by hand or with computer-aided design. Upper-limb devices fall into three categories: passive, body-powered and externally powered (myoelectric). Body-powered limbs work through a harness and cable attached to the opposite shoulder, while myoelectric arms respond to signals from the [[Muscle|muscles]]. Craniofacial, dental, breast and penile prostheses also exist, and an estimated third of upper-limb amputees worldwide use a passive prosthetic hand.

Sexual activity exchanged for payment, a form of sex work. The definition of sexual activity varies, but it usually requires physical contact with the customer, which also creates a risk of transmitting infections. Prostitution takes many forms, including street prostitution and escort prostitution, and brothels are establishments dedicated to it. Its legal status varies widely: it may be an enforced or unenforced crime, decriminalized, legal but unregulated, or regulated. A 2011 report by Fondation Scelles estimated about 42 million prostitutes worldwide and annual revenue over $100 billion. Some critics regard prostitution as exploitation that helps supply human trafficking and support the "Nordic model" that criminalizes the purchase of sex. Others regard sex work as a legitimate occupation, and Amnesty International calls for decriminalization. The word derives from [[Latin]] *prostituta*, but most sex-worker activists prefer the term sex worker.
